part.text:
Fixed. The regression came from commit 9cde7155 (#5540), which stopped rewriting imported tokens' `File` to a synthetic import-chain name. Since imported snippet tokens keep their original (earlier) line numbers in the same file, `isNewLine()` returned false at the splice point, so a nested `import` inside a snippet was never expanded and leaked into the parsed config as an unrecognized directive.

Changes (matching upstream fix in caddyserver/caddy#5626):
- `caddyconfig/caddyfile/lexer.go` — added `isNextOnNewLine(t1, t2 Token)` which, in addition to file/line comparison, treats tokens from different import chains (`Token.imports`) as being on different lines.
- `caddyconfig/caddyfile/dispenser.go` — `isNewLine()`, `isNextOnNewLine()`, `nextOnSameLine()`, and `NextLine()` now delegate to that helper instead of duplicating conditions.
- `caddyconfig/caddyfile/parse.go:467` — the snippet-detection loop in `doImport` now compares against `tokensCopy[i-1]` (which carries the just-appended import entry) via the same helper.

Validation: `TestNestedImport` (the FAIL_TO_PASS case reproducing this issue) and `TestImportErrorLine` now pass, and all compile-able packages in the repo pass their tests (the two `[setup failed]` packages fail identically on the unmodified tree due to missing offline module cache).
